subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
passage:
I'm Keerthana, the neighbour on the second floor. Last Saturday I was watering my balcony plants when a cricket ball crashed through the landing window below. Chaitanya, a boy of about ten, stood frozen with the bat. His father came out shouting, "What will the neighbours say? Get inside, don't tell anyone!" Chaitanya's face went grey. He scooped the ball, and glass stayed on the stairs.
All Sunday morning I saw him take the long way round, past the back gate. I don't know for sure what he was thinking. But that afternoon he knocked on my door and asked in a small voice if I would come with him to tell the watchman about the glass, before a small child stepped on it.

qa.q: What did Chaitanya's father shout after the window broke?
qa.a: He shouted, 'What will the neighbours say? Get inside, don't tell anyone!'

qa.q: What might Chaitanya have been feeling when his face went grey?
qa.a: He was probably afraid and embarrassed about being seen, though the narrator says the exact thoughts are not certain.

qa.q: What turning point shows Chaitanya thinking beyond fear of gossip?
qa.a: He knocked on Keerthana's door and asked Keerthana to come and tell the watchman about the glass so a small child would not step on it.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya's father have seen the broken window?
qa.a: He seems to worry more about what the neighbours will say than about the glass or the ball, so his first move was to hide it.

grounding: A child warned about what the neighbours will say fears public embarrassment before considering right and wrong.

subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
passage:
Monday: Elizabeth, eight, tore a page of a library book by accident. Mummy saw it and said quickly, "What will the librarian think? What will people say about us? Hide it in your bag." Elizabeth's stomach turned over.
Thursday: She took the long way to class so she wouldn't pass the library. When her friend Bhavna asked why, Elizabeth whispered, "Everyone will talk."
Tuesday: Bhavna said, "I tore a page once. Miss just gave me tape and said thank you for telling." She walked beside Elizabeth to the desk. Elizabeth put the book down with both hands and said, "This got torn, and I'm sorry."
The librarian reached for the tape.

qa.q: What did Mummy say to Elizabeth after the page was torn?
qa.a: She said, 'What will the librarian think? What will people say about us? Hide it in your bag.'

qa.q: What was Elizabeth feeling as she took the long way to class?
qa.a: She was afraid and ashamed of being talked about, fearing that everyone would know about the torn page.

qa.q: What made the difference on Tuesday when Elizabeth returned the book?
qa.a: Bhavna told a torn-page story of Bhavna's own and walked with Elizabeth to the desk, so Elizabeth could say sorry and hand the book back.

qa.q: How might Bhavna have seen Elizabeth's fear?
qa.a: Bhavna seems to understand it, having torn a page once too, and stayed beside Elizabeth to show that telling the librarian could be safe.

grounding: A child told what people will say learns to fear embarrassment before understanding right and wrong, until a friend eases it.
